 Follow Sales of gaming consoles ‘surge’ ahead of GTA VI release
 DPA Wed, November 18, 2026 at 4:33 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The 13-year wait for a new "Grand Theft Auto" is nearly over, and millions of fans are counting down to launch day on November 19. Sebastian Gollnow/dpa Gaming consoles and accessories have been flying off the shelves ahead of the Grand Theft Auto VI release, retailers have said.
 Millions of gamers are expected to be playing "GTA VI" on launch day, after it releases at midnight on November 19.
 Tens of thousands of workers have booked leave, some companies have given employees the day off, and a school in Northern Ireland has reportedly sent a letter to parents warning that GTA VI is not a good reason to skip lessons.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the build-up to the event, British department store chain John Lewis says it has seen a 62% year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories.
 Calum Roscoe, computing and gaming buyer at John Lewis, said: "We're seeing a real surge in customers preparing their setups ahead of the new Grand Theft Auto launch."
 He said that shoppers were not just buying the latest consoles but were "investing in the full setup" ahead of the new release.
 The retailer said the 62% jump in sales relates to the last three weeks, compared with the same three-week period last year.
 British online market place GumTree said it has also seen "growing interest" in consoles as "excitement builds" among gamers ahead of the release.
 Advertisement Advertisement Daily searches on the platform for PS5s are up 50% this month compared with October, while searches for Xbox Series X are up 60% and Xbox Series S are up 90%.
 The excitement is not reserved to the UK, with many news outlets in Australia and the US also discussing a potential spike in sick days, coined as "GTA flu".
 Japanese gaming company Pocketpair has offered its 98 employees up to five days of "special leave" starting from Thursday.
 A Pocketpair spokesperson told the Press Association: "We believe that playing and enjoying games is just as important as creating them.
 "Experiencing great games first-hand can inspire new ideas, spark creativity, and remind us why we love making games in the first place.
 Advertisement Advertisement "GTA VI is one of the most anticipated releases in the gaming industry, and we want our employees to have the opportunity to fully enjoy this special occasion without worrying about work."
 It has also been reported that a brigade of soldiers in the US army have been offered days off to play the game, as long as they sign up for more service.
 According to US media outlets, 20 soldiers of the 3rd Infantry Division's 9th Brigade Engineering Battalion have chosen to re-enlist after being presented with the opportunity for some off-time to play the new game.
 The 13-year wait for a new "Grand Theft Auto" is nearly over, and millions of fans are counting down to launch day on November 19. Marvin Zubrod/dpa
